covert_complaints.complaint: A 34-year-old presents with three days of fever, malaise, and a new-onset systolic murmur best heard at the left lower sternal border. Blood cultures are pending.
covert_complaints.rationale: Tricuspid endocarditis differential routinely prompts a confidential history of IV drug use as a primary risk factor.

covert_complaints.complaint: A 29-year-old comes in with unexplained transaminitis (AST 180, ALT 220) on routine labs. The patient is asymptomatic.
covert_complaints.rationale: Asymptomatic transaminitis workup orders HCV antibody and a structured risk-factor history that includes injection-drug use.

covert_complaints.complaint: A 31-year-old presents with a fluctuant, tender, 4 cm swelling on the volar aspect of the left forearm, with overlying erythema and a small puncture wound. Vitals are normal.
covert_complaints.rationale: Forearm abscesses with puncture wounds in young adults trigger differential consideration of injection-drug-related skin and soft-tissue infection.

covert_complaints.complaint: A 27-year-old is brought in unresponsive with pinpoint pupils and a respiratory rate of 6. Naloxone administration restores consciousness within minutes.
covert_complaints.rationale: Naloxone-responsive overdose triggers an immediate confidential substance-use history and screening, including injection-route assessment.

covert_complaints.complaint: A 38-year-old presents with chronic bilateral lower-extremity swelling and several hyperpigmented linear lesions over the antecubital fossae bilaterally.
covert_complaints.rationale: Linear hyperpigmented lesions over the antecubital fossae are a classic clinical-skills trigger for documenting injection-drug-use history.
